transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-02-18
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Samuel Ortiz (Elm Head of Cloud), Priya Desai (Elm CISO), Marcus Lee (Elm Eng Manager)

Auto-generated summary: discussed residency, HIPAA/GDPR, logging controls.

Topics: data residency, hosted vs dedicated vs private, logging restrictions, encryption/KMS, SOC 2 / ISO, pilot scope, timeline.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, and with me is Jordan our solutions engineer. How are you all doing?
[00:07] Samuel Ortiz: Doing well, thanks. We pulled in Priya and Marcus from security and engineering.
[00:11] Priya Desai: Hi all.
[00:12] Jordan Patel: Nice to meet you. Quick agenda — want to understand your compliance constraints and talk through hosted, dedicated, and private options and what folks typically choose for banks.
[00:21] Marcus Lee: Sounds good. We're primarily concerned with data residency and logging. We handle consumer financial data and a bunch of regulated flows.
[00:28] Samuel Ortiz: Yes, and we have EU customers so GDPR is a hard requirement; we also have internal rules to keep any PII off public clouds unless it's encrypted and proper contracts in place.
[00:36] Maya Chen: Totally. To set context, Redwood offers Hosted (our public API), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools with tenancy isolation), and Private (VPC/on-prem deployments). For banks like you, we usually see a mix: non-sensitive inference on Hosted, and sensitive workloads on Dedicated or Private.
[00:51] Priya Desai: On Hosted — what are the guarantees around residency? Can data be kept in a single region and is there any cross-region failover that would move data?
[00:59] Jordan Patel: Good question. For Hosted we can restrict region selection to, say, eu-west-1, but we do have control plane components that are multi-region for reliability. For strict residency for regulated data we generally recommend Dedicated or Private where you can pin everything to a region or your VPC.
[01:17] Priya Desai: We also have strict logging rules — logging of full request payload is not allowed, and audit logs need to be retained for seven years. Can Redwood support redaction or disabling of request logs?
[01:28] Maya Chen: Yes, we have configurable logging. For Dedicated and Private you can opt out of request payload logging and only keep metadata. We also integrate with customer KMS for key management so payloads can be encrypted at rest. On Hosted, we have retention policies, but it's not common to disable all payload logging unless you move to a Private setup.
[01:45] Marcus Lee: Can you clarify the KMS/HSM integration? We need FIPS-compliant HSM support for encryption keys.
[01:52] Jordan Patel: We support customer-managed keys via KMS in Dedicated and Private. For on-prem, we can integrate with HSMs — we have customers who use AWS CloudHSM or on-prem HSM appliances. I'll note that some transcripts/autogen sometimes call KV cache as KV cash, sorry — that was a joke — but the KV cache is separate from logs.
[02:11] Samuel Ortiz: That's helpful. What about model artifacts and weights — do they ever leave our region or are they hosted centrally?
[02:18] Maya Chen: For Dedicated you can host model files in your region or in your VPC storage. For Private deployments, all artifacts stay on your infra. On Hosted, model variants are served from our model catalog and may be pulled from multiple regions for performance, so not ideal if you require absolute residency.
[02:33] Priya Desai: GDPR also implies we need data subject access and deletion controls — do you have processes to support deletion of logs or user data on request?
[02:42] Jordan Patel: Yes, for Dedicated and Private we can implement deletion workflows and provide audit trails. On Hosted we can do deletions within retention windows but it depends on the contract; we can include stronger guarantees in enterprise terms.
[02:53] Maya Chen: Can I ask about scale and latency needs? That helps recommend Hosted vs Dedicated.
[02:57] Marcus Lee: We're expecting about 200 rps at peak for non-sensitive traffic and maybe 20 rps for sensitive flows. Latency target is sub-300ms p95 for critical customer-facing calls.
[03:08] Jordan Patel: For those numbers, Dedicated will give predictable throughput and latency. Hosted could work for the non-sensitive 200 rps if you can tolerate some variability. Private can hit low latency but requires more ops.
[03:19] Samuel Ortiz: Cost is also a factor — Dedicated reserved capacity is a commitment, what's typical pricing?
[03:24] Maya Chen: Pricing varies by capacity and model size. Typical pattern: start with Hosted for discovery/poCs, then move sensitive paths to Dedicated with reserved commits for unit economics. We can share a pricing worksheet post-call.
[03:34] Priya Desai: Any SOC 2 or ISO reports you can share? We need them for procurement.
[03:38] Maya Chen: Yes, I'll share SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 artifacts. Also our compliance kit includes penetration test summaries and a network architecture diagram.
[03:47] Marcus Lee: On the logging side, we have to ensure logs are only accessible to a small set of people and never leave our audit domain. Does Redwood support RBAC and integration with our SSO?
[03:56] Jordan Patel: Yes — RBAC, SAML/SSO integrations, and audit logs with retention controls are supported. In Dedicated and Private we can map roles to your IAM and supply read-only views for auditors.
[04:07] Samuel Ortiz: For GDPR data residency we also require data processing agreements and Standard Contractual Clauses (SCC). Are you able to sign those?
[04:15] Maya Chen: We have data processing addenda and are open to SCCs in our enterprise agreement. We'll include that in the legal pack.
[04:22] Priya Desai: A technical question — how do you handle prefix caching or KV cache so that cached states don't leak across customers? We need strict tenant isolation.
[04:31] Jordan Patel: We have per-tenant KV caches and for Dedicated/Private you can have isolated cache instances. On Hosted we use namespace isolation but guests have raised concerns, so for strict isolation Dedicated is the recommendation.
[04:43] Marcus Lee: For the pilots, would you run benchmarks with our data in your Dedicated environment or do we need to spin up Private?
[04:50] Maya Chen: We typically run a pilot in Dedicated where possible; we can also run a controlled benchmark with sample data in Private if you need absolute isolation.
[04:58] Priya Desai: What about retention of model outputs — some of our regs classify model responses as logs. Can you enforce retention policy per-route?
[05:06] Jordan Patel: Yes, retention policies can be route-specific in Dedicated/Private and we can redact or avoid persisting outputs altogether.
[05:13] Samuel Ortiz: Any gotchas around backups or snapshotting that might copy data out of region?
[05:18] Jordan Patel: Backups for Dedicated can be configured to stay in region; we'll provide a diagram for backup workflow. For Hosted some backups are multi-region for DR, so not suitable for strict residency.
[05:28] Marcus Lee: Ok. Another item — we have a compliance requirement for seven years of audit log retention and we need immutable logs. Can Redwood support WORM-like storage?
[05:37] Maya Chen: For Private we can configure WORM storage or push audit logs to your GCS/S3 with immutability policies. For Dedicated we can integrate with your long-term storage. We'll document options.
[05:47] Priya Desai: Great. Timeline — we're targeting a vendor decision by end of Q2 and pilot kickoff in early Q3. Is that feasible?
[05:55] Maya Chen: Yes that's feasible. We can aim to have the security pack over the next two business days and a demo/pilot plan by next week.
[06:03] Samuel Ortiz: Sounds good. Any concerns about model quantization or model variants affecting quality? We run some sensitive scoring models and want determinism.
[06:12] Jordan Patel: We can pin model versions and quantization profiles on Dedicated/Private. There's always some behavior change with quantization; we provide guidance and regression testing tied to eval suites.
[06:24] Maya Chen: Are there any other stakeholders we should include for the next meeting?
[06:28] Samuel Ortiz: Legal (procurement) will need to be involved once we have the security pack. Priya will lead on compliance. Engineering (Marcus) will validate the demo.
[06:37] Maya Chen: Great. Recap of action items: I'll send SOC2/ISO/network diagrams and legal templates; Jordan will setup a dedicated-demo environment and benchmark worksheet; Samuel will share sample dataset scope and retention rules.
[06:49] Priya Desai: Also request that logging of full request payload be disabled for the sensitive routes during the pilot.
[06:55] Jordan Patel: Noted — we'll show how to configure that and include it in the demo.
[06:59] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the materials and proposed times for the demo.
[07:03] Marcus Lee: Thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
